critique: The gold/orange particle rendering, black background, fine point density, and frame-to-frame fluid evolution are convincing. The mass is more centralized than before, but it still does not read as one cohesive drop: t1 contains several separated rolled lobes around a busy center, while t4 stretches into a ragged vertical plume with multiple curled protrusions and an open, broken interior. The Single Drop intent needs a denser, smoother, more unified core with less turbulent splitting.

suggestions.why: Higher fluid viscosity should hold the particles together longer, reducing the separated lobe structure and making the silhouette read as one denser drop.
Reducing vortex strength will lessen the strong rolling folds that tear the mass into multiple bulbous protrusions.
Lower X random swirl to reduce sideways fragmentation and keep the drop centered as it evolves.
Lower Y random swirl to prevent the tall, ragged plume-like breakup visible by t4.
Lower Z random swirl so the particle volume remains a coherent body rather than opening into multiple depth-separated curls.
